interpreter.name: Claude
interpreter.context: fresh session, no prior knowledge; only contact sheet and facts

object.short_description: Square stepped pyramid built from studded bricks: light grey/white terraces with four black central stair arms forming a cross in plan, topped by a small dark temple-like block with light openings.
object.construction_material: plastic building bricks (studded, black and white/light grey)

estimated_real_size.basis: bounding box 0.0959 x 0.0959 x 0.0715 in glTF metres; the base is about 12 studs wide with a stud pitch of about 5.5 % of the extent, i.e. about 8 mm, as in common brick systems

structure.overall_shape: stepped taper (truncated pyramid) with square footprint, four axial stair arms, small superstructure on top

components.name: stepped terraces
components.description: about eight receding square levels in white/light grey, each roughly 0.09 of the height apart; studs visible on the top faces

components.name: stair arms
components.description: black strips running from the base to the top on all four sides, forming a cross in the top view; the black bricks step up in a staircase profile

components.name: top structure
components.description: small dark block at the summit with light openings or lighter bricks on its sides, reading as a roofed shrine or temple chamber

components.name: base plate level
components.description: lowest wide light level (about 97 % of the footprint) that carries the stair arms and has the largest flat area

repeated_elements.what: round studs on the upward faces of the terraces

defects: thin diagonal lines on light surfaces suggest triangulated or merged brick faces
435 connected components, so the model consists of many separate bricks

evidence.statement: Four views from the sides show a symmetrical stepped taper with about eight receding levels.
The top view shows a black cross: one axial black stair strip on each of the four sides, meeting in the centre.
The surfaces carry round studs in a regular grid, and the model has 435 separate components, consistent with plastic building bricks.
A small dark block with light openings sits at the summit, reading as a shrine or temple.
Facts: footprint profile is a stepped taper (base ratio 0.966, top ratio 0.012), with 8 regularly spaced levels at a spacing of 0.09 of the height.
Facts: mirror symmetry about both horizontal axes is high, 4-fold rotation is medium, and mirror about up is low. The model is only roughly 4-fold symmetric.
Colours are only near-black (59 %) and near-white (41 %), with grayscale-like appearance (mean saturation 0.03).
The staircase on each side is a single central strip, narrow relative to the terrace width, and the summit block is small relative to the base (top ratio 0.012 for the topmost extent).
Extents are 0.0959 x 0.0959 x 0.0715, so height is about 75 % of the base width, which gives a fairly low pyramid.
The black strips are one stud-row wide stacked bricks with a stepped profile, so the stairs are steep and brick-built rather than carved into every terrace.

hypotheses.label: Pyramid-like monument with four stairs and a summit temple (brick-built model of a stepped temple-pyramid)
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: Many abstract stepped designs share terraces and a top block without representing any real monument.

feature_checks.feature: axial stairs on all four sides

hypotheses.label: Mesoamerican temple-pyramid (Maya or Aztec type) with a summit temple
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: Four-sided axial staircases and a small summit shrine also occur in Egyptian-style, Khmer or pure fantasy pyramids.

feature_checks.feature: small temple on a flat summit

hypotheses.label: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcan), Chichen Itza
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: The real building has 9 terraces, 91 steps per stairway and a wider stair, and the model shows about 8 levels with narrow stair strips and no distinct balustrades.

hypotheses.label: Other Maya pyramids (e.g. Temple of the Inscriptions, Tikal temples) or Aztec Templo Mayor type
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: These usually have a single front staircase, while the model has four of them.

hypotheses.label: Top structure as temple or shrine chamber with openings
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: The summit block is small and could merely be a decorative cap or a finishing brick stack.

hypotheses.label: Free design without a real-world model (generic brick pyramid)
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: The four-fold stairs and the summit shrine are specific features that make a deliberate reference to temple-pyramids likely.

feature_checks.feature: approximately symmetric build without irregular details

hypotheses.label: Egyptian-style or other non-Mesoamerican step pyramid (e.g. Djoser, Khmer temple mountain)
hypotheses.strongest_counterargument: Djoser has six steps and no stairs or summit temple, whereas the model has four axial stairs and a top structure.

questions_for_owner: Is the model based on a real monument or a game or film setting, and which one?
How many terraces and how many steps per stairway does the brick model have by design?
What do the light bricks on the top block represent (windows, doorway, decoration)?
Was the model built from physical bricks and scanned, or built digitally?
Is the black-and-white colour scheme intentional (for example reflecting limestone and shadowed stairs) or caused by available bricks?
notes: Hypotheses overlap and are not exclusive. The 435 components and stud grid favour a brick-built toy. Scale is an estimate based on a typical 8 mm stud pitch and may be wrong.
